mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-p1.title: Times tables
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-p1.body:
From the 3 times table, $3 \times 4 = 12$, so (E) is correct. The others mix up multiplying and dividing.

**Answer: (E) 12 = 3 × 4**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-p2.title: Count the zeros
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-p2.body:
One million is 1 000 000 (six zeros). 100 million is $100 \times 1\,000\,000 = 100\,000\,000$.

**Answer: (D) 100 000 000**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-01.title: Compare with 2000
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-01.body:
1902 is 98 below 2000, so 117 below 2019. 2190 is 190 above 2000, so 171 above 2019. 1902 is closer.

**Answer: (B) 1902**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-02.title: Count the small triangles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-02.body:
The large triangle is made of 16 small triangles (rows of 1, 3, 5, 7). 4 are white (the 3 corners and the middle one), so 12 are shaded. $\frac{12}{16} = \frac{3}{4} = 75\%$.

**Answer: (D) 75%**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-02.title: Count the white ones
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-02.body:
4 of the 16 small triangles are white: $\frac{4}{16} = \frac{1}{4} = 25\%$. So $100\% - 25\% = 75\%$ is shaded.

**Answer: (D) 75%**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-03.title: List the numbers
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-03.body:
The possible numbers are 54637, 45637, 46537, 46357 and 46375. The smallest is 45637, with the 5 after the 4.

**Answer: (B) after the 4**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-03.title: Think about place value
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-03.body:
To keep the number small, the 5 should go in front of the first digit that is bigger than 5. The first digit, 4, is smaller than 5, so keep it first; the next digit, 6, is bigger, so put the 5 before it: 45637.

**Answer: (B) after the 4**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-04.title: Start then finish
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-04.body:
There are 5 choices for the starting station, and then 4 choices for a different finishing station: $5 \times 4 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-04.title: Pairs, then directions
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-04.body:
There are 10 pairs of stations (Glasgow with 4 others, Stirling with 3 new ones, then 2, then 1). Each pair can be travelled in 2 directions: $10 \times 2 = 20$.

**Answer: (C) 20**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-05.title: Match the factors
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-05.body:
On the left: $10 \times 30 \times 50 \times 70 = (1 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7) \times 10\,000$. On the right: $1 \times 30 \times 500 = (1 \times 3 \times 5) \times 1000$. To match, the box must be $7 \times 10 = 70$.

**Answer: (D) 70**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-06.title: Share the border
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-06.body:
The area between the squares is $8 \times 8 - 4 \times 4 = 64 - 16 = 48$ cm². The inner square sits in the middle, so the border is made of 4 identical trapezia: $48 \div 4 = 12$ cm².

**Answer: (E) 12 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-06.title: Trapezium formula
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-06.body:
The trapezium has parallel sides 8 cm and 4 cm, and its width is $(8 - 4) \div 2 = 2$ cm. Area $= \frac{8 + 4}{2} \times 2 = 12$ cm².

**Answer: (E) 12 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-07.title: Bars eaten in an hour
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-07.body:
In one hour (3600 seconds) Britain eats $50 \times 3600 = 180\,000$ bars. The factory makes 2000 per minute, so it needs $180\,000 \div 2000 = 90$ minutes.

**Answer: (D) 90 minutes**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-07.title: Compare rates per minute
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-07.body:
People eat $50 \times 60 = 3000$ bars per minute, while the factory makes 2000. Eating is $1\frac{1}{2}$ times as fast, so one hour of eating needs $1\frac{1}{2}$ hours $=$ 90 minutes of making.

**Answer: (D) 90 minutes**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-08.title: Two kinds of edge
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-08.body:
Each triangle's 3 cm side lies along part of the next triangle's 8 cm side. So for each triangle, the outside of the shape uses its 7 cm side and the uncovered part of its 8 cm side, $8 - 3 = 5$ cm. Perimeter $= 6 \times (7 + 5) = 72$ cm.

**Answer: (C) 72 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-09.title: Steps of 7
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-09.body:
$2345 = 7 \times 335$, a multiple of 7. Then 2352, 2359, 2366 are 7, 14, 21 more — still multiples of 7. The next would be 2373, so 2374 is 1 more than a multiple of 7.

**Answer: (E) 2374**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-10.title: Count repeated letters
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-10.body:
CROATIA has 7 letters: A appears twice and C, R, O, T, I once each.
- ANDORRA: A twice, R twice — two doubles ✗
- FINLAND: N twice, F, I, L, A, D once ✓
- MOROCCO: O three times, C twice ✗
- URUGUAY: U three times ✗
- VIETNAM: all different ✗

**Answer: (B) FINLAND**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-10.title: Look at the pie slices
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-10.body:
CROATIA's chart needs one slice twice as big as the others plus five equal small slices (6 slices in all). FINLAND's chart has exactly this: a double slice for N and five single slices.

**Answer: (B) FINLAND**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-11.title: Parts
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-11.body:
Give Agnijo 1 part. Sam has twice as many: 2 parts. Naomi has three times Sam: 6 parts. Total 9 parts $= 180$, so 1 part $= 20$ and Sam has $2 \times 20 = 40$.

**Answer: (C) 40**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-11.title: Test the options
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-11.body:
If Sam has 40, Agnijo has 20 and Naomi has 120. $20 + 40 + 120 = 180$ ✓.

**Answer: (C) 40**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-12.title: Work step by step
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-12.body:
10% of the Camembert is 28 g, so the whole Camembert is $28 \times 10 = 280$ g. Half of it is 140 g. This is 20%, one fifth, of the Cheddar, so the Cheddar weighs $140 \times 5 = 700$ g.

**Answer: (C) 700 g**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-12.title: Stay with percentages
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-12.body:
Half the Camembert is 50% of it, i.e. $5 \times 28 = 140$ g. 20% of the Cheddar is 140 g, so 100% is $5 \times 140 = 700$ g.

**Answer: (C) 700 g**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-13.title: Check each mirror line
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-13.body:
- B is the logo reflected in a mirror line along its centre line (the two stems swap over, taking the circle and square with them).
- E is the logo reflected in a mirror line at right angles to the centre line.
- A and C are reflections in the two lines at 45° to the centre line.
- D: the circle and the square on the stems have been swapped, but the stems themselves have not been swapped. No mirror line does this, so D is not a reflection.

**Answer: (D)**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-14.title: Angles around S
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-14.body:
In a rhombus, neighbouring angles add up to 180° (opposite sides are parallel), so angle $PSR = 180° - 37° = 143°$. Each equilateral triangle has a 60° angle at $S$. The angles around $S$ make a full turn: $x = 360° - 143° - 60° - 60° = 97°$.

**Answer: (D) 97°**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-15.title: Add up all the moves
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-15.body:
Matthew uses every one of the 8 instructions once. Adding them all: North $1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 6$, South $2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 5$, East $1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 6$, West $2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6$. Altogether that is 1 square North. So he must start 1 square South of the Treasure: the middle square, "1S 1W".

**Answer: (E) 1S 1W**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-15.title: Follow the path
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-15.body:
Start in the middle (1S 1W) → bottom-left (1N 2E) → middle-right (1N 2W) → top-left (2S 1E) → bottom-middle (2N 1E) → top-right (1S 2W) → middle-left (1S 2E) → bottom-right (2N 1W) → Treasure. Every square is visited once ✓.

**Answer: (E) 1S 1W**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-16.title: Common factor
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-16.body:
The number of bunches must divide 21, 35 and 28 exactly. $21 = 3 \times 7$, $35 = 5 \times 7$, $28 = 4 \times 7$. The biggest common factor is 7: seven bunches of 3 white, 5 yellow and 4 red.

**Answer: (A) 7**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-16.title: Test the options
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-16.body:
12, 14, 21 and 28 don't divide 35 (or 21) exactly. 7 divides all three.

**Answer: (A) 7**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-17.title: Volume
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-17.body:
The rectangular tin holds $15 \times 24 \times 2 = 720$ cm³. The square tin has base $20 \times 20 = 400$ cm², so the depth is $720 \div 400 = 1.8$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 1.8 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-17.title: Compare base areas
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-17.body:
The base areas are 360 cm² and 400 cm². The same mixture spread over a bigger base is shallower by the factor $\frac{360}{400} = 0.9$: $2 \times 0.9 = 1.8$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 1.8 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-18.title: Ratio
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-18.body:
The sweets are shared $20 : 12 = 5 : 3$. So the ages are 5 parts and 3 parts, and their sum (8 parts) is a multiple of 8. It is also a multiple of 5, so a multiple of 40; less than 50 means 40. One part is 5 years: ages 25 and 15. Difference 10.

**Answer: (B) 10**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-19.title: Work out each square
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-19.body:
Let the large square have side 1 (area 1). The diagonal cuts it into two triangles.
- Bottom-left square: its corner touches the diagonal at the centre, so its side is $\frac{1}{2}$ and its area is $\frac{1}{4}$.
- Tilted square: it sits on the diagonal in the top-right triangle and its side is a third of the diagonal. Its area is $\frac{2}{9}$ (the triangle's area is $\frac{1}{2}$, split into 9 equal small triangles, and the square covers 4 of them).
- Corner square: it fills half of the small corner triangle, which is 1 of those 9 small triangles, i.e. $\frac{1}{18}$; half of it is $\frac{1}{36}$.

Total $\frac{1}{4} + \frac{2}{9} + \frac{1}{36} = \frac{9 + 8 + 1}{36} = \frac{18}{36} = \frac{1}{2}$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{2}$**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-19.title: Half of each triangle
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-19.body:
The diagonal splits the big square into two equal triangles. In the lower-left triangle, the shaded square fills exactly half (the triangle cuts into 4 equal small triangles and the square uses 2 of them). In the upper-right triangle, cut into 9 equal small triangles: the tilted square uses 4 and the tiny corner square uses half of 1, so $4\frac{1}{2}$ out of 9, which is again half. Half of each triangle is shaded, so half of the big square is shaded.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{2}$**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-20.title: Find a factor of 1000
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-20.body:
$1000 = 125 \times 8$. The product contains 125, and $124 = 4 \times 31$ and $126 = 2 \times 63$ give $4 \times 2 = 8$. So the product is a multiple of $125 \times 8 = 1000$ and ends in 000.

**Answer: (A) 000**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-20.title: Last digit
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-20.body:
The product contains 125 (a multiple of 5) and 124 (even), so it is a multiple of 10 and ends in 0. Only 000 ends in 0.

**Answer: (A) 000**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-21.title: Number line
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-21.body:
Put the ages on a number line: Kelly is halfway between John and Leo, and Leo is halfway between Kelly and Mila. So the gaps John–Kelly, Kelly–Leo, Leo–Mila are all equal. The picture is symmetric about the middle, which is the average of John and Mila: 11. Kelly and Leo are equally far from 11 on either side, so their average is 11 and their total is 22.

**Answer: (E) 22**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-21.title: Algebra
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-21.body:
$2K = J + L$ and $2L = K + M$. Adding: $2K + 2L = J + M + K + L$, so $K + L = J + M = 2 \times 11 = 22$.

**Answer: (E) 22**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-22.title: Middle square minus quarter circles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-22.body:
Join the centres of the four circles: they form a square of side 6 cm, area 36 cm². Inside it are four quarter-circles (one from each circle), which make one whole circle: 28.26 cm². The shaded region is $36 - 28.26 = 7.74$ cm².

**Answer: (C) between 7 cm² and 9 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-22.title: Whole square
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-22.body:
The big square is 12 cm across, area 144 cm². The four circles cover $4 \times 28.26 = 113.04$ cm², leaving 30.96 cm². This leftover is the shaded middle, 4 corner pieces and 4 edge pieces. A corner piece (a 3 × 3 square minus a quarter circle) is a quarter of the shaded middle, and an edge piece (a 6 × 3 rectangle minus two quarter circles) is half of it. So the leftover is $1 + 4 \times \frac{1}{4} + 4 \times \frac{1}{2} = 4$ times the shaded part, which is $30.96 \div 4 = 7.74$ cm².

**Answer: (C) between 7 cm² and 9 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-23.title: What each small hexagon adds
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-23.body:
Each small hexagon overlaps a corner of the large hexagon. The part of the large hexagon's edge hidden inside the small one has the same length as the part of the small hexagon's edge replacing it (the dashed rhombus shows both are two equal sides, and opposite sides of a rhombus are equal). What is gained are the two other sides of the small hexagon, i.e. $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$ of its perimeter. So the total perimeter is $60 + \frac{1}{3} \times 96 = 60 + 32 = 92$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 92 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-24.title: Total minus twice the overlap
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-24.body:
The overlap (white) is a right-angled isosceles triangle whose height is the rectangle's width, 3 cm, so its long side is 6 cm and its area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 3 = 9$ cm². The shaded area is the two shapes' areas with the overlap taken away from each: $36 + 24 - 2 \times 9 = 42$ cm².

**Answer: (A) 42 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-24.title: Each shape separately
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-24.body:
Shaded part of the square: $36 - 9 = 27$ cm². Shaded part of the rectangle: $24 - 9 = 15$ cm². Total $27 + 15 = 42$ cm².

**Answer: (A) 42 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-25.title: Three directions
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-25.body:
The box holds $5 \times 5 \times 6 = 150$ cm cubes, so everything fits exactly and the double cube can be anywhere. Count its positions by direction:
- Along one 5 cm edge: $4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120$ positions (4 places along the 5, any of 5 and 6 across).
- Along the other 5 cm edge: also 120.
- Along the 6 cm edge: $5 \times 5 \times 5 = 125$.

Total $120 + 120 + 125 = 365$.

**Answer: (B) 365**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-25.title: Count shared faces
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2019-25.body:
Each position of the double cube covers two neighbouring cells of the $5 \times 5 \times 6$ grid, i.e. one internal face between cells. Count internal faces in each direction: $(5 - 1) \times 5 \times 6 = 120$, $5 \times (5 - 1) \times 6 = 120$, $5 \times 5 \times (6 - 1) = 125$. Total 365.

**Answer: (B) 365**
